questions: Describe your undergraduate degree and major.
What specific aspects of AI do you find most interesting?
What projects, if any, have you completed that involved machine learning or data analysis?
Explain how embeddings help models understand data in your opinion?
Can you describe a time when you faced with a challenging problem during your studies that required you to think critically about how to approach it?
answers: I am currently studying Computer Science and I have mainly focused on learning programming fundamentals. During university I completed several assignments and a few small personal projects. I became interested in AI because I use AI tools regularly and wanted to learn how they work.

I am mostly interested in machine learning because I think it is one of the most common areas of AI. I would also like to learn more about chatbots and language models since they are becoming very popular. I am still exploring different AI topics to see which one interests me the most.

I have completed a few university projects related to machine learning and data analysis, but they were mostly focused on learning the fundamentals. One project involved using a dataset to train a simple classification model in Python. I learned how to prepare the data, split it into training and testing sets, train the model, and evaluate its accuracy.

I also completed a small data analysis assignment where I used pandas and matplotlib to clean data, generate basic visualizations, and identify simple trends in the dataset.

My experience is still quite limited, and I have not yet worked on large-scale machine learning systems or production AI applications. I am looking for opportunities to gain more practical experience through an internship.

My understanding is that embeddings help machine learning models represent data as numerical vectors that capture some of the relationships between different pieces of information. Instead of treating words or other inputs as separate items, embeddings allow the model to compare how similar they are.

For example, words with similar meanings tend to have similar embeddings, which helps the model process language more effectively. I know embeddings are widely used in natural language processing, although I have only learned the basic concepts and have not implemented embedding models myself.

During one of my university courses, I had to complete a small data analysis assignment using Python. At first, my code wasn't working because I had missing values in the dataset, which caused some errors during processing. I spent some time reading the error messages, checking each step of my code, and searching online for similar issues. Eventually, I realized I needed to clean the data before continuing with the analysis.

That experience taught me to solve problems step by step instead of changing many things at once. I also learned that reading documentation and understanding error messages can save a lot of time.

While their practical experience remains limited to smaller projects focused on learning fundamentals, they demonstrate a strong aptitude for problem-solving through iterative troubleshooting and clear logical thinking – exemplified by the detailed approach taken in their data analysis assignment.  They are eager to gain hands-on experience through an internship and possess the foundational knowledge necessary to contribute meaningfully to an AI engineering role.
